note: single_datetime_exposed is a submodule of single_datetime with no config, plugin, service or settings — just single_datetime_exposed_form_views_exposed_form_alter() (hook_form_BASE_FORM_ID_alter for views_exposed_form). It attaches the xdan datetimepicker (AttributeHelper::defaultWidget() + the single_datetime/datetimepicker library) to each exposed filter whose plugin_id is 'date' or 'search_api_date' AND whose value.type === 'date'; between/not between operators get the picker on both min and max (relabelled From/To). The medium/hard cases are grounded in real Views config: the exact keys the module tests (filters.<key>.exposed, .plugin_id, .value.type). IMPORTANT ENVIRONMENT NOTE: on this shared site an unrelated contrib module (search_api_taxonomy_machine_name) currently fatals Views filter-plugin discovery, so View::save() and exposed-form rendering are broken site-wide; therefore the setup/reset/verify scripts read and write the view config via the raw config factory (\Drupal::configFactory()/\Drupal::config()), which does not trigger handler discovery. The hard verifies assert the precise config conditions that cause the module to attach the picker; the intended agent action is to reach that config state (e.g. via drush config editing) rather than the Views UI, which is unavailable here.

evals.prompt: I enabled single_datetime_exposed on a Drupal site. What does it do to my Views, and what do I have to configure for it to take effect?
evals.expected_output: It automatically attaches the xdan jQuery datetimepicker to date-type exposed filters on every View, with no per-view configuration — it is a single hook_form_alter on views_exposed_form. You just enable it; any exposed date filter then gets the picker.

evals.prompt: Which exposed Views filters does single_datetime_exposed add the datetimepicker to? Be specific about the filter plugin ids and the value type it checks.
evals.expected_output: Only filters that are exposed AND whose plugin_id is 'date' or 'search_api_date' AND whose value.type is 'date' (absolute-date filters, not relative/offset ones). It skips Views live preview.

evals.prompt: How does single_datetime_exposed handle a Views exposed date filter that uses the 'between' (date range) operator?
evals.expected_output: For between / not between it applies the picker attributes to both the min and max sub-inputs and relabels them '( From )' and '( To )'; if only min is submitted it auto-fills max with min + 1 day so the range still filters. For other operators it applies the picker to the single input. It then attaches the single_datetime/datetimepicker library.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a View with machine id sdt_exp_known. Inspect its configuration and identify the exposed filter that single_datetime_exposed will enhance with the datetimepicker: give the exposed filter's identifier and why it qualifies.
evals.expected_output: The exposed 'created' filter, exposed identifier sdt_created, qualifies because it is exposed, its plugin_id is 'date' and its value.type is 'date'. Read views.view.sdt_exp_known display.default.display_options.filters.

evals.prompt: The View sdt_exp_which on this site has two exposed filters. Inspect its configuration and state which exposed filter (by identifier) single_datetime_exposed will attach the datetimepicker to, and which it will ignore.
evals.expected_output: It enhances the exposed date filter with identifier sdt_when (the 'created' filter, plugin_id 'date', value.type 'date') and ignores sdt_title (the 'title' string filter, plugin_id 'string'). Read views.view.sdt_exp_which filters.

evals.prompt: On this site the View sdt_exp_task has a date filter on the node 'created' field, but it is not exposed, so single_datetime_exposed does nothing. Make the change needed for single_datetime_exposed to attach the datetimepicker to it: expose that date filter (keep it an absolute-date filter). Apply the change to the live site. (Note: the Views UI is unavailable on this site because an unrelated module breaks Views filter discovery — edit the view configuration directly.)
evals.expected_output: In views.view.sdt_exp_task set display.default.display_options.filters.created.exposed to true (adding an expose section), keeping plugin_id 'date' and value.type 'date'. Do it via config (e.g. drush php:eval editing the config factory, or drush config:set), since the Views UI cannot render here.

evals.prompt: On this site the View sdt_exp_abs has an EXPOSED date filter on 'created', but it uses a relative/offset value (value.type = offset), so single_datetime_exposed skips it. Change that exposed filter so single_datetime_exposed will attach the datetimepicker — it must be an absolute-date filter (value.type = date). Apply the change to the live site's view configuration.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.sdt_exp_abs set display.default.display_options.filters.created.value.type to 'date' (keeping exposed true and plugin_id 'date'). Edit the view config directly since the Views UI is unavailable on this site.
